display.title: Episode 479: The Big Barrel of Wine (Rosh Chodesh Sivan)
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan, Uncle Yossi explains why the whole world was created for the sixth of Sivan, and tells the story of the townspeople who each poured water instead of wine.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, a few days before Shavuos. Uncle Yossi explains Rashi's teaching on 'Yom HaShishi': the extra letter hei points to the sixth of Sivan, the day the Torah was given, for which the whole world was created. To prepare, we resolve to learn more Torah and to do mitzvos with yiras Shamayim, carefully and exactly as Hashem commanded, like checking that every letter of a mezuzah is perfect, and to accept the Torah with joy. After the Hakochainik march, two sisters from a Brooklyn girls' school say the Shema and one of the Twelve Pesukim, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time tells of the merry winemakers of a town famous for its wine. To welcome the king, each family is to pour a gallon of wine into a giant barrel, but one by one everyone thinks 'my water won't be noticed', and the king's golden cup fills with plain water. The show ends with a reminder that everyone, young and old, should come to shul on Shavuos to hear the Aseres HaDibros.
display.lesson: Never say 'let someone else do it': do your own share of every good thing and set an example for others.

date.note: 'Today is the first day of the new month... Sivan'; Shavuos 'this coming Sunday' fits 6 Sivan 5751 = Sunday 19 May 1991. A Tuesday.
